slot.brief: Given a complex like Co(NH3)5Br(SO4), identify the type of isomerism (ionisation/hydrate/linkage) and which pairs actually show it.

stem: Which pair of coordination compounds consists of ionisation isomers?

verdicts.working: Ionisation isomers differ by exchange of a coordinated ion and a counterion. In (A), coordinated Br⁻ and outer-sphere SO₄²⁻ exchange positions; the other pairs show linkage, hydrate, and coordination isomerism, respectively.

working:
A: $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]^{2+}/\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ and $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]^+/\text{Br}^-$ exchange the coordinated anion and counter-ion.

Independent check: Ionisation isomers differ by exchange of a coordinated ion and a counterion. In (A), coordinated Br⁻ and outer-sphere SO₄²⁻ exchange positions; the other pairs show linkage, hydrate, and coordination isomerism, respectively.
solution: Ionisation isomers differ by interchange of an ion inside the coordination sphere with a counter-ion outside it. In (D), coordinated $\text{Br}^-$ and outer-sphere $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ exchange positions, giving $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ and $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Br}$.
